text:
alex: Heads-up — since last night we've been seeing a recurring p99 regression (approx 1.6s -> 2.1s) in the crux-eu2 dedicated pool during the nightly batch window (02:00-03:30 UTC). Pattern looks like co-located batches + MIG sibling SM saturation.

maria: Seeing the same on our side, noticed CPU on the host jumped and KV cache miss rate increased. Is this the batch job you mentioned (crux-analytics)?

alex: Yes, crux-analytics kicked a large batched embedding job at 02:05 UTC. It landed on host-n7-gpu-03 where we also have fractional MIG slices for other tenants. Quick paste of sampling from our monitoring: 

```
Host: host-n7-gpu-03
Slice: MIG-1 (3g,7gb)
time=2026-03-16T02:12:04Z p99=2100ms sm_util=93% l3_bw_util=87% kv_cache_miss_rate=0.42
time=2026-03-16T02:14:08Z p50=120ms p95=780ms p99=2000ms queue_wait=18ms
```

jamal: @alex can you share the exact instance and slice IDs? If this is a packing issue we might need to repro by forcing placement.

alex: slice id is "slice-03a" on host-n7-gpu-03. Attached the allocation snippet from scheduler: 

```
allocation {
  pool: crux-eu2
  host: host-n7-gpu-03
  slice: slice-03a
  tenant: crux-analytics
  model: embedding-large-v2
  started_at: 2026-03-16T02:04:58Z
}
```

zoe: Quick triage: can you run a snapshot of SM utilization and KVS lock stats while the job runs? Also check if autoscale bumped or throttled slices.

alex: ran a quick snapshot (attached below). Looks like the autoscaler did not trigger a scale-up because total pool free slots were 0, so queueing started instead of adding more nodes.

```
> rwi infra snapshot --host host-n7-gpu-03 --since 2026-03-16T02:00
SM_util: 88-94% across slices
PCIe_bw_util: 70%
KV_cache_hits: 58% KV_cache_miss: 42%
Autoscale_action: none (pool free_slots=0)
```

maria: That KV miss rate is concerning — if the embedding job thrashes the KV cache it will cause tail amplification for co-resident slices. Could be L3/SM interference plus cache eviction.

ops-oncall: tagging @eng-runtime and @eng-infra - can you confirm whether this host has any placement constraints that prevented spreading? Also, is there a config that forces fractional MIG packing that is too aggressive? :eyes:

infra-bot: Autoscale history:
```
2026-03-15T23:50 - scaled down -1 node (policy: cost-window)
2026-03-16T01:30 - no scale action (min_nodes met)
```

jamal: Things to try / immediate mitigations:
- Move crux-analytics batch off host-n7-gpu-03 (temp host drain)
- Bump pool min_nodes by +1 for the nightly window
- Add soft anti-affinity rule for large-batch tenants during 02:00-04:00 UTC

zoe: For reproducer steps: start a parallel large-batch embedding job pinned to slice-03a while running a light latency-sensitive model on sibling slice. Measure p99 on the latency-sensitive model. Use this shorthand: 

```
# start batch job (stresser)
rwi job submit --tenant crux-analytics --model embedding-large-v2 --batch-size 2048 --target-slice slice-03a
# start probe (latency-sensitive)
rwi job submit --tenant test-probe --model chat-small --rate 1/s --target-slice slice-03b --collect p99
```

alex: I can run the repro in staging tonight and will paste logs. If @eng-runtime confirms this is MIG sibling interference we should add an automated placement rule to avoid co-hosting large batch jobs with low-latency tenants.

maria: Agreed. Also recommend we add a dynamic scaling policy that considers recent KV cache miss rate and SM_util as signals for scale-up (not just queue length).

jamal: Filing an internal incident ticket and assigning to eng-runtime + eng-infra. I'll include the snapshots and the suggested repro. Ticket: INF-2026-2843.

zoe: Thanks — tagging the crux account via support case so they know we're investigating and suggesting they throttle batch parallelism for now. :thumbsup:

alex: Will follow up with the staged repro and time-aligned traces. Thanks all.
